sense.text:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning”: the things written before time are the Bible. They were written for us to learn from, to examine how our forefathers operated, good or bad.

“That we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” We examine what our forefathers went through in the scriptures so that we can have hope in today’s time, to endure and go through the same. This is how we should view the state of our people: blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans in a state of decay, much of it sparked by integration with the other nations, the same thing that happened to us in every captivity before.

precepts.why:
“For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. The scriptures tell us to inquire of the former age and search out our fathers, through the Bible and also in this captivity.

Look back just fifty years and blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans are in a worse state than they were then. We are in a state of decay, a state of decline. We glorify degeneracy, we glorify sin.

“For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth are a shadow”: we have a short time on this earth and know nothing. That is the same thing Romans 15:4 says, that the things written before time were written for our learning.

“Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, and utter words out of their heart?” The former age and the search of our fathers shall teach us. In the scriptures we see how our forefathers integrated with the other nations and fought to be around them in every captivity, and how it sent us into decay and decline as a nation. The same thing has happened in this one.

sense.text:
Some ask what was wrong with integration, and say we are better off today. God is not about integration. God is all about segregation, and many of our people do not realize it.

“And the seed of Israel separated themselves from all strangers, and stood and confessed their sins, and the iniquities of their fathers.” You see it all the time throughout the scripture: the seed of Israel separated themselves. God was all about separation.

precepts.why:
Some will say we are under Jesus now, that God so loved the world. Nothing changed in the New Testament: “Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate”. The same thing read in the Old Testament is read in the New.

The “them” in the context of the chapter is the unbelievers, those in idolatry, and that is the other nations too. When we attach ourselves to the other nations, all their doctrines and philosophies come along with it, and we want to be like them in all things.

“Saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you”. God has always been about segregation.

“Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.” There it is again, what Job 8 and Romans 15 said.

“When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance”: divided. God has always been about each nation staying with its own nation. “When he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel.”

“For the Lord’s portion is his people”, and God’s people have always been the Israelites. So God is always about segregation. What has happened is that we envy the other nations, look at what they do, and want to be attached to them, and that further pushes the decline you see in the black community.

sense.text:
God told us this in ancient times, like Romans 15:4 says about the things written before time. In the old days only eight percent of children were born out of wedlock, because if you got pregnant they sent you down south to your grandmother’s house.

“Thus saith the Lord, Stand ye in the ways, and see”: you have to stand in the ways and see what we have become since we integrated and left off from learning the things of old. Look at us as a nation, not at the one-off situations, not at the one who says he was raised with his whole family.

“And ask for the old paths, where is the good way”. How did we used to do it back in the day? The old paths are the good way. Things have gotten worse as we have progressed and integrated into society, but the old ways of our grandmothers and grandfathers were the good ways where you had a little bit of peace.

“And walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls.” As much as we have progressed in technology and integrated ourselves into society, we have lost rest for our souls as a people. We work longer hours and two jobs; our families are disoriented and destroyed, a mother raising two or three kids by herself, a father paying child support for two or three kids. These new ways have destroyed us.

“But they said, We will not walk therein.” Get that old stuff out of my face, we say, and look what it has done to us. Brothers and sisters, get back to the old ways, which are God’s ways.

Integration caused black wealth to decline. Yes, we are in captivity because we broke God’s commandments, and part of breaking his commandments is our need to integrate with the other nations. But even in captivity God still commanded us what to do.

“Now these are the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem unto the residue of the elders which were carried away captives, and to the priests, and to the prophets, and to all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away captive”. In our captivity these words were sent to Israel.

“Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them”. Even in captivity we were told to build houses. It takes a level of economics, of money, to build houses and plant gardens and eat the fruit of them. Even in captivity we were commanded to be sufficient: come together, build houses, sustain yourselves.

“Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters”: have a family. “And take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands”. That builds a nation, a society, a community, even in captivity.

“That ye may be increased there, and not diminished.” Increased in captivity. And the sons and daughters were given among themselves, to their own race of people. It was never go take sons and daughters of the other nations.

“And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the Lord for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace.” God commanded us even in captivity to sustain ourselves, come together, build houses, plant gardens, take wives and build family. That is the structure of a nation and a community.

We did try to do these things: banks, schools. But because we wanted to integrate, Esau came in and tore all of it up. J. Edgar Hoover, the director of the FBI, said the worst thing for American society was negro unity, because they understand that when we unify as a nation the one thing that has to come in is the Bible, and then everything they built is destroyed. Integration was nothing but a modified form of segregation, to break our people down into small groups and control their minds. When we come together and prosper as a nation of people, they look at it as an invasion: there goes the property value, there goes the neighborhood. And there is a major highway driven right through every black community, by design.

The basic rule in economics is that you spend your money in your own community and make it bounce many times before it leaves. Black money never bounces once. Our forefathers always understood to keep things within us.

“Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them”. Today that would be real estate: they took their houses, put them on the market and sold them. “And brought the prices of the things that were sold”.

“And laid them down at the apostles’ feet: and distribution was made unto every man”. That money stayed within the community, among us. You always see these principles in the Bible. They had all things common, and that is why none of them lacked.

You saw it with Black Wall Street, where a dollar circulated for months before it left the community. But because we want to integrate with the other nations and love them so much, we take our money and keep it with them, and our communities continue to decline.

Between 1888 and 1934 there were 134 black-owned banks in the United States, over sixty of them prosperous in the first decade of the 1900s, before integration, giving loans for homes and businesses that white-owned institutions denied. Esau came in and called them speculative investments, and then came the racial violence, the destruction of Black Wall Street in Tulsa: the negroes are prospering more than us, drop a bomb on them.

“Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds!” This society, this nation has devised iniquity. They go to sleep thinking about evil and wake up thinking about evil, how to destroy and keep blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans destroyed.

“When the morning is light, they practise it, because it is in the power of their hand.” Because we broke God’s commandments, they have the power to come against us, to destroy us economically and systematically when we try to build a nation. It was so powerful they did not only infiltrate it; they said blow it up, flood it.

“And they covet fields, and take them by violence; and houses, and take them away”. That is blowing it up. In the early 1900s they blew up Black Wall Street and flooded Lake Lanier, and there are many black towns where they did the same, and look at them today. They did it to the Northern Kingdom too.

“So they oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage.” The purpose of it is to oppress a man in his house and his heritage, to cause him to integrate, to come to them.

precepts.why:
They come in with their policies and a crafty counsel. “And through his policy also he shall cause craft to prosper in his hand”: through his democracy, through his policies, he causes craft to prosper.

“And he shall magnify himself in his heart, and by peace shall destroy many”. They make you think it is peace: the Great Society of 1964, Lyndon B. Johnson’s plan, I am coming to help the impoverished and the poor. Why are they impoverished and poor? Because you bombed their city, flooded their lake and put bills and policies in place to make them poor.

That is how we went from 134 black banks to about 23 in 2025, some of them online with no building, and the FDIC does not even call them banks but minority depository institutions. A black bank only needs 51 percent of the voting stock owned by black people, so the other 49 percent is Esau and the other nations. Through his policy he causes craft to prosper. It was more than Black Wall Street: Greenwood, the Hayti District in Durham, Harlem, U Street in Washington, 10th Street in Oak Cliff, Dallas, a thriving black community then and the hood today.

sense.text:
It was not only black people. Hochatown in Oklahoma was a thriving Gadite community of the Choctaw, what society calls the Native Americans, which is Gad according to the Bible. The Choctaw Nation passed laws to keep timber among its own citizens and keep the other nations out: negroes were not to sell timber to non-citizens, keep it among us. They sold lumber to the blacks and kept it within. Blacks on one end and Native Americans on the other were coming together, and Esau wants you to think they were separate and not dealing with each other. Then the allotment process, the United States government signing a law that let whites come in and take Gadite land, put it into private hands, white hands, and the Dierks brothers’ lumber company moved in to reap the benefits.

“He hath put forth his hands against such as be at peace with him”. He comes screaming peace. “He hath broken his covenant”: every treaty they had with the so-called Native Americans, he broke every last one of them.

“The words of his mouth were smoother than butter”: we will take your land and make it prosperous and give you this. You saw it in Killers of the Flower Moon and all throughout Oklahoma. While they were destroying Judah at Black Wall Street they were destroying the so-called Native Americans. The Trail of Tears pushed them to Oklahoma, they set up shop and began to prosper, and Esau came in and infiltrated, stole, raped, robbed and pillaged.

Esau puts loopholes in his documents so that Gad does not understand the language, and then gets you with that same document. The words in his documents were smoother than butter, “but war was in his heart”. The Edomite is the damn devil. And it shows that when we integrated with the other nations it was to our destruction.

“His words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.” They say white settlers came in and brought industry, that schools were built because of the white man, that the timber ran out so the town moved on. The timber is not gone: the company is still there, the largest owner of softwood timber in the world, with eighteen-wheelers of lumber leaving day and night. The first Hochatown was flooded to make Broken Bow Lake; under that lake is a city, where Gad was. And now the Choctaw you see advertised there are white: they oppress a man and his heritage. Everybody thinks Oklahoma is Gadite country, but in over ten years here you can count on one hand the real Gadites you have seen; they pushed Gad further west. This is the home of the five-dollar Indian: they infiltrate and then call themselves the Indian, the real Indian, superior over the red man.

“Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemy. Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked”. That is what we see: the secret counsels of the wicked, who devise iniquity. “From the insurrection of the workers of iniquity”.
“Who whet their tongue like a sword, and bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words”.

“That they may shoot in secret at the perfect”. That is why you do not hear about this history; they try to keep it secret and hide it. But God has sent his prophets on the earth to reveal it, to reveal that son of perdition that worketh iniquity. The perfect are God’s chosen people, the Israelites.

“Suddenly do they shoot at him, and fear not.” They are not afraid of what they are doing, not afraid of God’s judgment for trying to destroy his chosen people.

“They encourage themselves in an evil matter”: they take pride in destroying us and keeping us destroyed. “They commune of laying snares privily; they say, Who shall see them?”

What you do not realize is that integration was a snare, devised by our enemies, and the second point of it was that it destroyed the black family structure. This is why Trump is removing the history out of the museums: he knows that history is so dark, and they want to keep us ignorant that we were once a thriving people in this country.

“Marriage is honourable in all”. Not fifty years ago, even in this captivity, we believed marriage was honourable; that is why only eight percent of children were born out of wedlock, where today it is seventy-five percent. The Bible is all about marriage, and that is something we have forgotten in the black and Hispanic community.

“And the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.” We have become whoremongers and adulterers, and God said he will judge. Before integration we had a sense of family and marriage with our own nation, our own people.

Society has made living without the husband easy. Welfare is not the best thing, and teenage pregnancy cannot be stopped by programs; it has to be morals, and morals come from God. The programs were put in place to cause teenage pregnancy, so that you lose the sense that marriage is honourable.

These are the morals of God. “That the aged men be sober, grave, temperate, sound in faith, in charity, in patience.” Notice it starts with the man. That is the order, the structure of a family: it starts with the father in the house and then trickles down.

“The aged women likewise”: just like the husband, because she is learning from her husband. “That they be in behaviour as becometh holiness”, which we do not see in our society today. “Not false accusers, not given to much wine”, and our women are drunk, some still from last night.

“Teachers of good things”: those are the morals. They are to teach their children how to conduct themselves, how to love themselves, how to move as a man or woman of God.

“That they may teach the young women to be sober”, sober minded. “To love their husbands”: the black woman has to be taught how to love her husband, and society has not taught it and will not teach it. Before integration the black woman had some sense of how to love her husband, which is why she was the least divorced; we lost that because we want to be like the other nations, and they do not move like that.

“To love their children”. Integration caused that to collapse. Now the woman would rather the TV, BET, TikTok, Instagram and the streets love and teach her children.

“To be discreet”: you teach your daughters to conduct themselves, not all up in men’s faces. “Chaste” means sexual purity, your virginity means something. In the neighborhood a virgin gets scorned and shunned, and that is not normal to God. We did not have the commandments, but before integration we had a sense of that.

“Keepers at home”. Mothers and grandmothers knew how to make food stretch; now we are a microwave society. “Good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.” Husband, husband, husband: this is the family unit. These were the morals that had to be taught. Then came the welfare state and the Great Society, plans they said were to help low-income urban neighborhoods, and all it did was destroy us further and take us further from what God commanded.

Black women were more likely to be married than white women until 1970. Up until 1960 only five percent of black women thirty-five and older had never married: they were wives and mothers, not baby mamas, side pieces or video vixens. Then the welfare state came, integration came, and it spiked. Esau thinks long term and puts his policies in place to see what will happen ten and fifteen years later.

Our foremothers were always about raising their children, being keepers at home and teachers of good things. Here is a married woman who taught her children.

“But she bowing herself toward him, laughing the cruel tyrant to scorn, spake in her country language on this manner; O my son, have pity upon me that bare thee nine months in my womb”. She “endured the troubles of education.” We think programs are supposed to teach our children and prevent bad behavior. No, it is the morals of God, what we read in Titus 2: teaching the young women to be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, and the young men to be sober minded and like their father. She is instructing these young men to be like their father.
“I beseech thee, my son, look upon the heaven and the earth, and all that is therein, and consider that God made them of things that were not; and so was mankind made likewise.”

“Fear not this tormentor”: do not fear your enemy, give glory to God. This is how you train up your children. Our people had a sense of that before integration: they knew who the enemy was and were taught to love themselves and their nation.

“But, being worthy of thy brethren, take thy death”. She told her son to take his death. How many women can say that to their child?

precepts.why:
Another example of her children. “After him was the third made a mocking stock: and when he was required, he put out his tongue, and that right soon, holding forth his hands manfully.” He had just seen his brothers killed.

“And said courageously, These I had from heaven; and for his laws I despise them; and from him I hope to receive them again.” Where did he learn that? She endured the troubles of education: it was instilled in him by his father and his mother, the family unit, the family structure.

“Insomuch that the king, and they that were with him, marvelled at the young man’s courage”. Do not think he just learned that; that courage was instilled in him from his youth. We saw it before integration: black teachers, a mother and father in the household, everything us, and it gave us a sense of unity and purpose.

“But the mother was marvellous above all, and worthy of honourable memory: for when she saw her seven sons slain within the space of one day, she bare it with a good courage”. Where was that instilled in her? From her husband. And she bare it “because of the hope that she had in the Lord.”

Integration was a direct attack on that black unity and black family structure, because the family structure instilled in us a sense of us and helped us understand who our enemy was.

sense.text:
In the black community we were prepared with goals and morals in the home, the church and the school, and the schools were not integrated. One woman said her segregated school was the best school experience of her life, because all her teachers were negro. Her third grade teacher wrote the first book of negro history for children, and her seventh grade teacher wrote a book too. Look how old she is and she still remembers their names.

“For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image”. Image is crucial to us as a community, and our enemy understood that. Integration destroyed that image. She saw people like her in positions, an image to look at that said she was not just nothing.

There is nothing wrong with wanting teachers and influencers that look like you. It gives you comfort and relatability. Do not let the other nations call you a separatist for it; they feel comfortable with their own people too. God made every race on earth. And it was a close-knit community: if you misbehaved in school, the teacher stopped by the house on the way home. That is a nation, a family structure that starts in the household and branches out into the schools.

Back then children got a whipping. We integrated and wanted to start disciplining our kids like Esau. No, discipline your kids the way God said to. And it is not the crazy, extreme stuff.

“He that loveth his son causeth him oft to feel the rod”, the rod of correction and rebuke, “that he may have joy of him in the end.” So when he grows up he is not a drug dealer; he has a sense of morals and the fear of God.
“He that chastiseth his son shall have joy in him, and shall rejoice of him among his acquaintance.”

“He that teacheth his son grieveth the enemy”. It is not beating him to a pulp out of frustration because you feel you cannot control him; that is abuse. It is the rod and correction, and teaching.

The other nations understood this, and that is why integration was pushed on our people. That sister, Barbara Sizemore, became a teacher and a writer, one of the first black women to head the public school system of a major city, Washington DC. Where did she see that? From her third and seventh grade teachers, the image in front of her. He that teacheth his son grieveth the enemy, and integration was set to destroy and dismantle all of that. “And before his friends he shall rejoice of him.”

“Though his father die, yet he is as though he were not dead”. It is as though the father did not even die, because his son comes up in his stead. Everything the father had he poured into his son, and now the son is a replica and an example of his father: “for he hath left one behind him that is like himself.” That is what we saw in 2 Maccabees 7; you know that household had a father in it, and the mother was teaching them.

“While he lived, he saw and rejoiced in him”.

The beginning of nationhood is the family: man, woman, children. “For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall be joined unto his wife, and they two shall be one flesh.” This is marriage, a husband and a wife.

“This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church.” The same dynamics you see in a household between the husband and the wife represent how Christ dealt with the church, the body, the nation of Israel.

Nationhood starts in the house, with the family: how a woman deals with her husband, how a husband deals with his wife, how they deal with the children. All that trickles down, and then a bunch of families come together and build a nation. That teacher who stopped by the house had a husband and children too.

What we have to do is get back to the Bible and apply it in our lives; that will change the trajectory of our nation and build it back up.

“For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people”. We have been hard-headed since the day God brought us out of the land of Egypt.

“But in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.” That is why there is so much opposition to what we teach on the streets and on every platform: the powers that be are trying to keep us from remembering ourselves. Once we remember who we are in this Bible, we will get back to applying its principles, and our situation will change in a generation: more marriages, sons growing up with fathers, daughters with mothers who teach them how to conduct themselves.

Do not let anybody tell you your history and your past mean nothing. If that were so, the other nations would teach their kids to forget theirs. They are built on the principles of their ancestors and told to become better, everyone except us, because they know who we are and how much better it would do us as a nation. To this day they still teach that George Washington chopped down a cherry tree.

With the welfare state, the Great Society, Section 8 and the rest came the Universe 25 experiment of John B. Calhoun in the 1960s and 1970s: an enclosure of pens where mice were given food, water and nesting boxes, everything needed to survive, like food stamps and WIC. Overcrowding led to social breakdown: the mice became aggressive and hostile, mothers abandoned their young, infanticide became rampant, which is what we call abortion today. They attacked each other, not the one who put them there. Some, the beautiful ones, withdrew from society to groom and eat, like the women on TikTok and Instagram. Put a picture of the experiment next to an aerial view of the projects and they look the same. Esau devised iniquity: break up the family structure, overpopulate these areas with housing, Section 8 and food stamps, and they will decline.

“Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” God told us to be separate from the other nations and choose none of their ways. We chose to integrate and choose all their ways, and you see the fruits of it.

“By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery”. Is that not happening in our communities? “They break out, and blood toucheth blood.” Esau understood that: overpopulate the blacks and they will kill each other. We hate one another, attack one another, kill one another, and glorify killing.

“Therefore shall the land mourn”. Over and over you see black women crying because their son was shot and killed. “And every one that dwelleth therein shall languish, with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of heaven; yea, the fishes of the sea also shall be taken”.

“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge”: our people are destroyed for lack of God’s commandments. “Because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee”. We go into the slums and the ghettos where our people are and tell them to keep God’s commandments, and many reject it. God said because you reject knowledge, I will reject you. There is no father in those households; the black family structure has been destroyed, and Esau understood he could do it through integration.

You saw the experiment with the rats, and immediately the correlation with man. “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.”

Without the laws of God, man will always resort to his lower nature: violence, killing each other, killing his babies. That is why the laws of God are so important, that we follow them to the best of our ability and do not act on the flesh. Esau knows this: give it to black folk, the man is gone, they have no laws to discipline them, and they will be just like the mice in that maze.

People see us on the streets and on social media and ask why we are so angry. If you see what our women and men have become, with no order and no structure as a people, and you are not angry, you are part of the problem. Five more years down this road and we will be worse off than we are now.

“Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad”. If you are not mad, God says you are a fool. If you are okay with your people living like this, aborting their babies, in prison and killing each other, you are a fool, because that would have made a wise man so mad he would have done something: let me teach them what God says. As that lady said in 1986, nothing will change our community or teenage pregnancy except the morals of God.

Now the women teach their children to be in survival mode: be tough, do not express yourself. That is not survival; that is stuck on stupid, on a road to destruction, crash test dummies. This is the image our black women and daughters have now. Esau is playing on a whole other field when it comes to blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans, and only God’s laws can save our people.

“Behold, every one that useth proverbs shall use this proverb against thee, saying, As is the mother, so is her daughter.” The mother teaches her daughter all her ways, through her example, what she says and how she moves.

“Thou art thy mother’s daughter, that lotheth her husband”. You see it in our community today: the black woman hates the black man.

“And thou art the sister of thy sisters, which lothed their husbands”. The Northern Kingdom is not exempt; you move the same way.

“As for my people, children are their oppressors”. These youngins in the streets gang banging, overly aggressive, hostile, the one with a bottle for every op: it was by design.

“And women rule over them”, because there is no father in the home, and if there is one, he is weak, a simp. “O my people, they which lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths.” That is what you see among our people. Integration was detrimental: it collapsed the black family structure through their policies and procedures.

The third point: unemployment of black men skyrocketed with integration. Black wealth declined, the family structure declined, the man cannot be in the household because of AFDC, WIC and Section 8, there are no more black businesses, and he cannot find a job. All of this pushed our people further into a state of decay.

“Let him that stole steal no more”. That is what happens when you cannot find a job: a man begins to steal, rob and murder. “But rather let him labour”: you counteract stealing by working. Esau understood: destroy the black family and the black businesses so there is no money among them, and with nothing to turn to they will rob, steal and kill one another, and crime will skyrocket.

precepts.why:
All these things come from wanting to be among the other nations, which is why the seed of Israel separated themselves.

“Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me”. Solomon is praying: give me enough, what is convenient for me.

“Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord?” You see it among our people: some reach a high status, pulled out by Esau and paid millions to keep us destroyed, and being full they deny God. I am rich, I am not in poverty.

“Or lest I be poor, and steal”. When you are poor you are more inclined to steal, and Esau understood that. Keep the black men unemployed and they will steal, and then push them right into the prison. Take them out of their own schools, where the teacher would tell your parents, and put them in integrated schools where the teachers do not care about them; they grow up to be thugs, cannot get a job, and steal, kill and murder. They have us in a trick bag.

sense.text:
They choose where to build prisons by predictive modeling: they take third grade reading scores, and if enough kids in a zip code cannot read at grade level by age eight, that neighborhood gets flagged, not for support but for future incarceration. They do not send tutors; they send architects.

“They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search”. That is what we saw with the Universe 25 experiment and the same thing here. The whole search is to shoot at the perfect in secret and lay snares for the poor.

“Both the inward thought of every one of them, and the heart, is deep.” Every one of the so-called white man, Esau, thinks long term. They know if they break up the family, tear down black wealth and keep black men from jobs, he will steal, rob and murder, and leave the same example for his children.

“But this is a people robbed and spoiled”: Israel, a people robbed and spoiled. “They are all of them snared in holes”: the policies and the things set up against us are the snares and holes.

“And they are hid in prison houses”. The same system that teaches us in elementary school until we are grown men has us hid in prison houses, because it has been programmed into our minds. A mother says she is teaching them to survive; no, you are teaching them to be beasts in the streets.

“They are for a prey, and none delivereth”. They do not send tutors, they send architects. Even the renaissance they promise, rebuilding the hood, is not for black people. Gentrification is not for you.

The fourth point was the myth of a colorblind society. They do not mean you cannot see color; they want you blind to your own color, your heritage. And they do it through their Christianity, their policies, integration. Now we want to be in their churches and among them, and they hate our guts.

“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.” They use that to deceive you into thinking God is colorblind, so everybody has to be around each other. They read John 3:16 and negate Matthew 15:24. Christ was speaking to nobody but his people.

precepts.why: “But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” Christ was sent to his nation, his people. So the world he was talking about in John 3:16 was the Israelites.

Yes, we go to the Old Testament. We do not care what you think, you dumb apologetics: Christ taught from the Old Testament. “But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation”. Israel shall be saved. Does everlasting end? No.

“Ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.” They will say you have to go to the Greek, the Septuagint, the lexicon, the other translations. The everlasting life of John 3:16 is the everlasting salvation of Israel.

Our forefathers understood who the world was. They were not colorblind.

“Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there”. Christ raised Lazarus from the dead, “Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.”

“For this cause the people also met him, for that they heard that he had done this miracle. The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him.” What did the Pharisees call the Jews? The world. They understood who the world was.

“And there were certain Greeks”. Those Greeks were among the Jews counted as the world. But Christianity wants you colorblind to your own race, to forget who you are as a nation, and to look at them as your god whose ways are pure while you are nothing but a gentile who should be happy they took you from the shores of Africa and civilized you. Christianity programmed our people to demonize our own heritage and give up our name, identity and tongue to fit into their squares, circles and triangles, to hate ourselves and how we look.

sense.text:
They put their image up, the image of the beast, and everything you see in it is right, good and holy, so you think white is right, not realizing Christ looks like you.

“His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow”. That image does not have woolly hair. Blacks and Hispanics have woolly hair. If our people understood that Christ had hair like theirs, they would be more conscious of their own hair texture and not bleach it, blonde it and perm it to oblivion. They fry it, dye it and lay it to the side till there is no more left to fry. A sister had a perm at two years old, when the hair follicle is not fully developed and the baby still has a soft spot. That shows the level of self-hatred integration caused: hating ourselves and loving their wealth, their images and their traditions.

“And his eyes were as a flame of fire”.

“And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace”. The color of Christ’s skin was like fine brass burned in a furnace. That is a black man.

To all you pathetics who will be watching this class: we give you life; there is no reason for you to wake up unless we are doing the work of God. Break down all of that symbology, the similitudes of his hair and his feet of brass, the long garment, the golden girdle, the red eyes. All of that is the symbology of his glorified state. You never break it down; you just say he is not black. We will break it down then. The challenge is on you pathetics.

All of this causes us to love the glory of the other nations more than ourselves, and you see the same thing in history. “But after the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus, called Epiphanes, took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest”. This was the Greek captivity: he went underhand to his oppressors to become ruler over the people.
“Promising unto the king by intercession three hundred and threescore talents of silver, and of another revenue eighty talents”: he promised the king money.

“Beside this, he promised to assign an hundred and fifty more, if he might have licence to set him up a place for exercise”. He got a licence, a permit, for a place of exercise, promising even more revenue. That place of exercise is what you see today with our people: the gymnasium, the ball, the football field, glorifying their traditions.

“And for the training up of youth in the fashions of the heathen”. You see the same today in the policies put in place. In the black neighborhoods the YMCAs and after-school programs were taken away and replaced with basketball courts and remodeled football fields. That is training them up in Greek fashions, and it all started right after segregation, when they enforced integration.

“Not setting by the honours of their fathers, but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all.” That is what you see with our people, and what Christianity teaches us. Integration made a so-called colorblind society, which is not colorblind; it is blind to your own color. And color is not a crayon in the box: it is your own nation, your heritage, your traditions, this Bible, traded for liking their ways best of all.

“By reason whereof sore calamity came upon them”. You see that in our community today: the Christian church has been in the black community for hundreds of years, and we have only gotten worse and worse. “For they had them to be their enemies and avengers, whose custom they followed so earnestly”. We earnestly follow their pagan holidays, like that wicked Halloween last night, and Christianity does not speak against it; they bring it into the church.

“And unto whom they desired to be like in all things.” Our people desire to be like the other nations in all things: our women blonde their hair, black men dress a certain way, they join the Greek fraternities.

Not only that, we take wives of the other nations. The myth of color blindness teaches you to hate yourself and your people and love them.

“My son, keep the flower of thine age sound”. The flower of your age is your wife, and your wife is to be a woman of your nation, not a strange woman. “And give not thy strength to strangers”: you are not to give your strength to strangers, marrying women of the other nations.

“When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed”. Integration and Christianity taught us that God loves everybody, everybody is a child of God, be with whoever you want. The Bible says sow it with thine own seed, “trusting in the goodness of thy stock.” We had a sense of that fifty years ago and in the early 1900s; we stayed among each other.

“So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified”. God is all about race, all about nations staying with their own race and nation. That is how your race is magnified: keep the flower of your age sound and sow your seed among your own. They want you to believe we are all equal, but integration was just a modified form of segregation used to continue to destroy you.

The fifth point: the black community became dependent, because of the lack of the laws of God. Love thy neighbor as thyself is gone, marriage is not honourable, we have no school systems of our own. God said it would happen.

“Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”: we are to serve the Lord in all things.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee”. Because we did not, we serve our enemies, and God sent them against us. “In hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”: everything we want, we go to the other nations for. If they cut off the water or shut down the grocery stores, our people do not know what to do; you saw some of it in COVID. Today is November 1st: you wanted to integrate so bad, you got the food stamps and thought it was good, and now they cut them off. Now what are you going to do?

“And he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” When he took our heritage and nationality and beat it out of us, he took the yokes of iron off, because we were destroyed as a people.

“As for us, our eyes as yet failed for our vain help”. We look to the other nations, and God says it is vain help. “In our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save us.” This nation cannot save us, yet time and again we want to integrate, be among them and equal with them, thinking they have our best interest at heart. No. Everything they have done has been to destroy the black and Hispanic man and woman, northern and southern kingdom. They cannot save us, nor do they want to.
“They hunt our steps, that we cannot go in our streets”. You see it all throughout our communities, and still we look to a nation for vain help.

“Turn ye unto him”: that is what we must do, turn to God. “From whom the children of Israel have deeply revolted.” Deeply. We see the depths of our revolt in how much we love the other nations. Examine the state of blacks and Hispanics today: we are lawless and degenerate, taught to hate everything about ourselves and to love and embrace everything this system has set up for us. It all stems from not wanting to keep and apply the commandments God has given us.

Everything we went through today you see examples of in the Bible, written before time for our learning. Nehemiah was cupbearer to the king. He saw the state of his people and made his request: “So I prayed to the God of heaven. And I said unto the king, If it please the king, and if thy servant have found favour in thy sight, that thou wouldest send me unto Judah, unto the city of my fathers’ sepulchres, that I may build it.”

“For how long shall thy journey be? and when wilt thou return? So it pleased the king to send me; and I set him a time.” This also shows you dumb apologetics that Isaiah 14 did not happen in the Persian and Median captivity: why would Nehemiah have to ask the king he worked for for leave, if they were already back in the land possessing it?

Nehemiah understood segregation, being separate from the other nations, and here you see the spirit of how the other nations move; they do the same thing today. “Then went I up in the night by the brook, and viewed the wall”, and “the rulers knew not whither I went, or what I did”.

“Ye see the distress that we are in, how Jerusalem lieth waste, and the gates thereof are burned with fire: come, and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem, that we be no more a reproach.” He saw the distress of his people. “And they said, Let us rise up and build. So they strengthened their hands for this good work.” They came together as a nation to have their own.

“But when Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian, heard it, they laughed us to scorn, and despised us, and said, What is this thing that ye do? will ye rebel against the king?” The other nations see us building and laugh us to scorn.

“The God of heaven, he will prosper us; therefore we his servants will arise and build: but ye have no portion, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.” You, the nations, have no business among us, no business building with us, no business being part of us. Nehemiah understood segregation was what was beneficial for our people, and that these heathen are nothing but trouble.

“When Sanballat heard that we builded the wall, he was wroth, and took great indignation, and mocked the Jews.” He got mad because they built. Any time we come together as a nation and want to build something and stop the degeneracy in our neighborhoods, the other nations get mad and mock us, and sometimes they pay our own people to do it.

“What do these feeble Jews? will they fortify themselves?” Esau thought the same when he emancipated us: these feeble Jews. But we began to build, come among each other and unify, and we had a better economic system and more prosperous towns and cities than they did. This is the spirit of the other nations: they destroy us and then mock, are these feeble Jews going to build? “Will they make an end in a day? will they revive the stones out of the heaps of the rubbish which are burned?”

“Now Tobiah the Ammonite was by him, and he said, Even that which they build, if a fox go up, he shall even break down their stone wall.” Whatever they build a fox can break down; they will not come up out of that rubble without us. That is because Nehemiah had told them they had no portion nor right in Jerusalem.

“Hear, O our God; for we are despised”. To this day we are despised when we try to wake our people up out of their decayed state, rebuild the breach and change the minds of our people. “And turn their reproach upon their own head, and give them for a prey in the land of captivity”.

Now there was dissension among our own people. “And there was a great cry of the people and of their wives against their brethren the Jews.” Some said their sons and daughters were many and they needed corn to eat and live; some said “We have mortgaged our lands, vineyards, and houses, that we might buy corn, because of the dearth.” They mortgaged their houses and land because of the hard times. Others said “We have borrowed money for the king’s tribute”, to pay their taxes.

“Then I consulted with myself, and I rebuked the nobles, and the rulers, and said unto them, Ye exact usury, every one of his brother.” The nobles and rulers were in cahoots with the other nations and robbing the people, exacting usury that made them poor. It is the same today: we integrated, and now some of us in the Christian churches, the politicians, the Boule, exact usury and press our people to make us poorer.

“We after our ability have redeemed our brethren the Jews, which were sold unto the heathen; and will ye even sell your brethren?” We just redeemed them from the heathen and you want to sell them back? “Then held they their peace”: they had nothing to say, because they knew they were wrong.

“Restore, I pray you, to them, even this day, their lands, their vineyards, their oliveyards, and their houses”. He told the nobles to give it back, because it was all about us being together and having all things common.

This is the kind of leader Nehemiah was: “I and my brethren have not eaten the bread of the governor.” He did not exact usury like the nobles; he understood nation building.

“But the former governors that had been before me were chargeable unto the people”. That is why the people had waxed poor and mortgaged their lands to pay their taxes, the same as our people today. Nehemiah would keep it in house: “but so did not I, because of the fear of God.” He saw the decay of his people and went to build.

“Moreover in those days the nobles of Judah sent many letters unto Tobiah”. The nobles of Judah were the bourgeoisie, the Herodians you read of in the New Testament. Tobiah was of the other nations, “and the letters of Tobiah came unto them.” Many in Judah were sworn unto him: they wanted to be integrated with the other nations.

Nehemiah was all about segregation, because he saw what integrating with the other nations did to our people: a decayed estate, robbed and destroyed. That is why he told Sanballat and Tobiah they had no portion with us.

Nehemiah got the other nations out, kept the dollar within, restored the people’s lands from those in league with the other nations, and restored nationhood. Then he had to go back, because he was only on leave for a time.

“On that day they read in the book of Moses in the audience of the people; and therein was found written, that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God”. These nations were not supposed to be among us either, “Because they met not the children of Israel with bread and with water, but hired Balaam against them”.

“Now it came to pass, when they had heard the law, that they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude.” They still had other nations coming among them.

“And before this, Eliashib the priest, having the oversight of the chamber of the house of our God, was allied unto Tobiah”. Nehemiah segregated them and left, and what did they do? They integrated again. “And he had prepared for him a great chamber”, where the tithes commanded for the Levites were laid; he took what was supposed to go to the Levites and gave it to the heathen.

“But in all this time was not I at Jerusalem”. While he was gone, the bourgeoisie had allied with them because they wanted to integrate so bad. Integration was always a detriment to our people in Nehemiah’s time and always caused us to go back into sin, the same as in this captivity. Esau studies how the nations dealt with us throughout history to see what he can use to keep us destroyed.

When he got leave and came back: “And I came to Jerusalem, and understood of the evil that Eliashib did for Tobiah, in preparing him a chamber in the courts of the house of God.” The Bible calls it evil.
“And it grieved me sore: therefore I cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah out of the chamber.” He cleaned it all up.

When he came back they were integrated again, bringing the heathen into the chambers of the house of God and giving them the provision for the Levites. “In those days also saw I Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab: And their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews’ language”. They did not even know their own language. As that child grows up he teaches his child the same, and now your whole tradition has been integrated to be like them, no longer like you. That is the whole purpose of it.

“Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? yet among many nations was there no king like him”. King Solomon sinned by marrying wives of the other nations. From Nehemiah to the Greeks to now, integration has always been a detriment to our people.

precepts.why:
It is the same thing back in chapter 4: “And our adversaries said, They shall not know, neither see, till we come in the midst among them, and slay them, and cause the work to cease.”

That is the whole point: they want to come in among us, destroy us and cause the work to cease. That was the whole purpose of integration. Back then we had a sense of unity and purpose and understood who the enemy was, and they understood that if the commandments of God came in, it would be a detriment to them. So they broke it all up, because they want the work to cease.

sense.text: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”. We are not desired by the other nations; anything they put in place is to destroy us and not for our benefit. That is why we must come together in these last days, and the way we come together is under God’s laws, statutes and commandments.

“Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff”. In these last days we must gather ourselves together and be about ourselves: blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans under God’s commandments.

“Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” We must not envy the oppressor. We have to move through this society, but we do not have to be integrated with them or bring them into our circle. We have to be about our people.

We must gather ourselves together and come back as Israelites under the law, statutes and commandments. “They said one to another, Let us restore the decayed fortune of our people”. That is what we must do. We see the decayed estate of our people, destroyed through integration and all these policies and procedures, and we must come back to God’s laws and begin to restore. That is why we are on the street corners teaching our people to repent and keep God’s commandments, and why we have programs in place.

“And let us fight for our people and the sanctuary.”
